narrative: Your application was denied because the prediction estimated an 81.8% probability that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. That is a high-risk estimate, not a certainty, but it was strong enough to lead to rejection. The most influential factor was your third-year class standing: you are in the lowest decile, while accepted students average around the sixth decile. This pushed the prediction strongly toward bar failure. The second most important factor was your first-year class standing, also the lowest decile versus an accepted-student average near the sixth decile; it also pushed toward failure. The third factor was your family income bracket. Being from an upper-middle-income family is common among accepted students and slightly pushed toward passing, but it was not nearly strong enough to offset the academic signals. The prediction therefore treated your early and later class standing as the clearest indicators of bar-exam risk. To improve your chances, focus on strengthening your academic record and bar-exam readiness, seek advising from admissions and pre-law staff, consider targeted LSAT preparation or a retake, and reapply once you can show a more competitive record and evidence of sustained improvement.
